parts.title: My grandmother's bakery
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
My grandmother has a small bakery in the old part of town. It opened in 1985, and it has hardly changed since. The same wooden counter is there, and so are the same blue tiles on the wall. People come from all over the city for her chocolate cake.

When I was ten, I started to help her on Saturday mornings. At first I only washed trays, but she soon let me mix the eggs and the sugar. She never uses a machine. "Your hands know how long to mix," she says. I did not believe her until I made my first perfect cake.

The secret of the cake, she says, is the chocolate. She buys the best in the shop, even if it is expensive. She also puts a spoonful of coffee in the mixture. "You cannot taste it," she says, "but it makes the chocolate stronger."

Next year, I will leave for university, and I am afraid that I will miss the bakery. My grandmother just smiles and says that she will keep a piece of cake for me whenever I come home.

questions.explanation: She never uses a machine; your hands know how long to mix.

options: Good chocolate and a little coffee
Fresh eggs and a lot of butter

questions.explanation: She buys the best chocolate and adds a spoonful of coffee.

options: Sure of a job in the shop
Afraid he will miss the bakery
Worried that she will have to sell it
questions.explanation: He is afraid that he will miss the bakery.

parts.title: The story of chocolate
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There are three extra sentences.
parts.passage:
Chocolate comes from the seeds of the cacao tree. [1] Today, we think of it as a sweet food, but it was not always so.

The first people to use cacao were the Maya, in Central America, more than two thousand years ago. [2] They mixed the seeds with water and chilli to make a bitter, spicy drink.

When Spanish explorers arrived in the sixteenth century, they took cacao home to Europe. [3] They added sugar, which made the drink much sweeter, and soon it became fashionable among the rich.

The first solid chocolate bar appeared in England in 1847. [4] Before that, people could only drink it, and it was too expensive for most families.

Today, chocolate is made all over the world. [5] Experts say that each person in some countries eats about eight kilos of it a year.
sentences: The seeds are dried in the sun for about a week.
It was one of the most important events in the history of food.
The tree grows only in warm, wet places near the equator.
It was so valuable that they used the seeds as money.
Some people cannot eat it because of an allergy.
In Switzerland, chocolate was first mixed with milk in 1875.
People never seem to get tired of this sweet food.
At first, Europeans did not like the taste.

gaps.explanation: The tree grows only in warm places, which leads on to how we think of chocolate today.
The seeds were so valuable that they were used as money, and the next sentence says what the Maya did with them.
At first Europeans did not like the taste, so they added sugar.
The first chocolate bar was one of the most important events, and the next sentence says before that people could only drink it.
People never get tired of this sweet food, and the next sentence gives how much people eat.

She made a bit of a mess, [4] she was very proud of herself. Could you send me the recipe for the chocolate sauce too? I think it would taste lovely [5] the cake. I will bring you a piece [6] I see you at school on Monday. Best wishes, Clara

parts.title: Too many sweets?
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage: Many children love sweets, but eating too many is bad for your teeth. Dentists say that it is not only the sugar, but also how often we eat sweet things, [1] matters. If you eat sweets all day, your teeth have no time to recover. It is better to eat them after a meal, [2] you have more saliva in your mouth. Drinking water also helps to wash away the sugar. You should brush your teeth [3] least twice a day, in the morning and before bed. Some sweets are better than others. Dark chocolate, [4] example, has less sugar than milk chocolate. The worst sweets are the sticky ones, [5] they stay on the teeth for a long time. Remember, you do not have to stop eating them completely. You just need to [6] careful.

gaps.explanation: It is how often we eat sweet things that matters: a cleft sentence.
After a meal because you have more saliva: a reason.
At least twice a day: a fixed phrase.
Because they stay on the teeth: a reason.
Need to be careful: the infinitive of be.

parts.title: A talk at a chocolate factory
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note. Write one or two words, a number, a date or a time.

turns.speaker: nathalie
turns.text: Welcome to our chocolate factory. My name is Carys, and I will be your guide today. We make about twenty thousand bars every day. Last year it was fifteen thousand, and when the factory was small it was only two thousand, so you can see that we have grown. We send our chocolate to forty countries. Some people think it’s more, perhaps fifty, because they see our bars on holiday everywhere, but it’s forty. The factory was started in nineteen twenty by a farmer called Mr Hale. It was nineteen twenty, not nineteen thirty as some websites say, and it was in the little building on your left, which is now our shop. Now to the cacao beans. They arrive from Ghana, in big bags, every month. Before, we bought them from Brazil, but now Ghana is better for our recipes. Some beans also come from Peru, but only for our special bars. Then there is the mixing. The mixture is stirred for three days. I know it sounds like a very long time. Other factories do it in one day, and a few famous brands stir for five, but we think that three days gives the smoothest taste. You can watch the machines through the big windows. Finally, the tasting. At the end of the tour, you can try five kinds of chocolate: milk, dark, white, orange and chilli. Most visitors choose milk, but I recommend the chilli. Please do not touch the machines, wear your hair net all the time, and stay with me, because the floor can be slippery. Now, let’s go and see the first room.

gaps.explanation: They make about twenty thousand bars a day; it was fifteen thousand last year.

gaps.prompt: Number of countries that buy the chocolate: ___
gaps.explanation: Some people think fifty, but it is forty countries.
It was started in nineteen twenty, not nineteen thirty.

gaps.prompt: Country that supplies the cacao beans: ___
gaps.explanation: The beans now arrive from Ghana; they came from Brazil before.

gaps.prompt: Days that the mixture is stirred: ___
gaps.explanation: The mixture is stirred for three days; other factories use one or five.

gaps.prompt: Kinds of chocolate to taste at the end: ___
gaps.explanation: Visitors can try five kinds: milk, dark, white, orange and chilli.

parts.title: An interview with a pastry chef
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Colm, how did you get your job at the hotel?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: People expect a story about a cooking contest, and I did enter one once, but I lost in the first round. And I didn’t study abroad either, I’ve never left this country for more than a week. I started at sixteen as a kitchen helper, washing pots and carrying flour. The chef noticed that I got up early and never complained, and he gave me small jobs in the pastry corner.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Your chocolate fondant is famous. Why is it special?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: It’s not the cheapest, in fact it’s one of the most expensive desserts on our menu, because of the quality of the chocolate. And there is no secret sauce, only a little cream. What makes it special is that it’s warm and runny in the middle. When you cut it, the chocolate flows out onto the plate. Guests always smile at that moment.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What’s the hardest part of your work?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Timing, no question. A fondant needs exactly eleven minutes. One minute more and it’s a normal cake, one minute less and it’s soup. Washing up is boring but easy, and buying food is a pleasure, I love going to the market. But timing wakes me up at night, even on holiday.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Why do you eat cheese and fruit at home?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: People imagine my kitchen is full of cakes, and I know my family would love that. Pasta and bread are fine, but no. After ten hours with sugar and butter, I’m tired of sweet things. I don’t want to see a cake. And money isn’t the reason, my salary is good.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What do you do on your days off?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: I don’t visit restaurants, I see enough kitchens during the week, and I don’t sleep all day, though I’d like to. I go hiking in the hills with my dog. It’s quiet, it’s the opposite of the kitchen, and it clears my head.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What advice would you give to a young cook?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Be patient and curious. Don’t expect to be a chef in a year, it takes time. Ask questions, try new things, taste everything. And don’t be afraid of mistakes, I make them too. A burnt cake teaches you more than ten perfect ones. If you can’t make mistakes and never ask why, you won’t learn.
